questions.stem: The saturation pressure of ether is 400 Torr at 17°C. With an enclosure of V = 20 L, what is the maximum mass of ether that can be vaporized at 17°C? Molar mass of ether 74 g. (R = 8.31 SI)
(Continued) What is the ether vapor pressure at 17°C of this mass if the volume of the enclosure increases by 5 liters?
questions.explanation: Same amount in 25 L: P = 400 × 20/25 = 320 Torr.

questions.stem: One liter of aqueous solution contains 11.1 g of CaCl₂ (M = 111 g/mol) and 45 mL of H₂SO₄ (1 mol/L). The electrolytes are totally dissociated. Calculate the osmolarity of the solution.
questions.explanation: CaCl₂: 0.1 mol × 3 = 300 mosm; H₂SO₄: 0.045 × 3 = 135 mosm; total 435 mosm/L.

questions.stem: Estimate, in atmospheres, the osmotic pressure of a solution of osmolarity 0.104 osmol/L at 27°C opposed to pure water by a semipermeable wall.

A dialyzing membrane separates 2 compartments (A) and (B) of fixed and equal volumes containing aqueous NaCl solutions at equilibrium. In (A), the equivalent concentration is 170 mEq/L. A fully dissociating protein RNa₁₅ is then introduced into compartment (B). At this moment, compartment (B) has a freezing-point depression of −0.67°C. Given K = 1.8 (SI), determine the molar concentration of this protein before dissociation.
questions.explanation: Osm(B) = 0.67/1.8 ≈ 372 mosm/L; NaCl gives 340 mosm/L, so the protein adds ≈ 32 mosm/L = 16 particles × c → c = 2 mmol/L.
